dishes.name: Brandade de Nîmes
dishes.desc: Salt cod poached and worked with olive oil, milk and garlic into a smooth purée. Recipes in Nîmes date back to 1786, and it is the city's best-known dish.

dishes.name: Gardiane de taureau
dishes.desc: Camargue bull meat marinated in red wine and slowly stewed with vegetables and condiments, usually served with rice. Eaten in Nîmes and the Camargue, especially in winter.

dishes.name: Petit pâté nîmois
dishes.desc: A small pastry created in 1800, filled with minced veal and pork, some versions with brandade. A common lunchtime snack at the covered market.

dishes.name: Croquants Villaret
dishes.desc: Crunchy dry almond biscuits made in Nîmes by one family firm since 1775, flavoured with honey, orange blossom and lemon.

dishes.name: Pélardon
dishes.desc: A small AOC goat's cheese from the Cévennes, eaten with bread or with honey and dried fruit. The Gard's best-known cheese.
